the 5-HTTLPR genotype is associated with harm avoidance, but not neuroticism, and that the effect is moderated by the personality questionnaire used, with the TCI/ TPQ showing an association that is not present for the NEO.
The serotonin transporter (5HTT) gene is associated with anxiety-related traits, especially when measured by the TCI/ TPQ harm avoidance scale, but not with the NEO neuroticism scale.

the role of the serotonin transporter (5HTT) gene in anxiety-related traits.
the role of personality inventory in moderating the association between 5HTT genotype and anxiety-related traits.
the association between the 3’-untranslated region (3’-UTR) polymorphism of the 5HT transporter gene and personality traits.

, at present, there is little evidence for an association between the serotonin gene and anxiety-related measures, and the effect of personality inventory is not significant.
the association between the 2-allele variant of the 5HTTLPR and anxiety-related personality is small and may not be robust.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a weak but consistent effect of the serotonin transporter gene on anxiety-related personality traits, and that this effect is more apparent in the TCI/TCQ harm avoidance scale than in the NEO neuroticism scale, although the latter result was not significant.
there is some evidence that the 5HTTLPR polymorphism influences personality and that the effect is more apparent for TCI/ TPQ harm avoidance than NEO neuroticism.

the 5HTTLPR gene is associated with personality traits in some studies, and not in others, but that there is no evidence to suggest that this is due to differences in the type of measurement instrument used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the serotonin transporter gene is a poor candidate for anxiety-related traits.
there is no clear and consistent pattern of results that would suggest that personality inventories moderate the association between 5HTT and anxiety-related traits.
the association between the 3′-UTR polymorphism in the serotonin transporter gene (5-HTTLPR) and anxiety-related personality measures may be small, if present at all.
